events.body: judge escalates → human review: segment finding undetermined for F3
certificate: ✓ RD-1 off-route segment(s) exist [case] 2 segment(s) (F3, F4)
✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F3] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (no evidence)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:59:30 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. This is a metered RydeTAXI trip with two measured off-route segments, F3 (14:59–15:05, 3.56 km driven vs 1.74 km optimal, +1.82 km) and F4 (15:16–15:23, 4.21 km driven vs 1.57 km optimal, +2.63 km); each is reviewed under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 and any segment not exempted is refundable under RD-2 [F3][F4][RD-1]. Segment F3: at 14:56 the driver asked "Jam on Pan Island Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Bukit Batok West Avenue 3?" and at 14:56 the rider replied "Sure, no problem." — a rider message, in a complete and fully timestamped chat, sent before the 14:59:30 segment start [F9][F10][F11][F3][RD-5]. Because the trace treats that finding as outcome-relevant, the case goes to a person.

claims.assertion: The GPS track records two off-route segments on this metered RydeTAXI trip: 14:59–15:05 adding 1.82 km (F3) and 15:16–15:23 adding 2.63 km (F4), totalling 4.45 km of detour on a trip whose optimal route is 18.7 km (F1); each segment is an 'off-route segment' that must be reviewed under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 (RD-1).

The first segment (F3, starting 14:59) is covered by the rider's own consent: at 14:56 the driver asked 'Jam on Pan Island Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Bukit Batok West Avenue 3?' (F9) and the rider replied 'Sure, no problem.' (F10) — a timestamped message (F11) sent before that segment started, i.e. a specific named-road agreement that reaches only the first detour (RD-5).

The first segment is also justified by traffic: PIE (the optimal corridor) was at speed band 4, 30–39 km/h, during 14:44–15:34 (F13), consistent with the jam the driver cited when asking at 14:56 (F9), so nothing is refundable for that first segment (RD-4, and RD-3(a) as a rider-named stop/reroute).

The second off-route segment (F4, 15:16–15:23, +2.63 km) was never put to the rider: the complete chat record contains only two messages, the driver's 14:56 question and the rider's 14:56 reply (F9, F10, F11), neither of which concerns the 15:16 segment, and the driver's own statement concedes 'The second turn-off was my GPS rerouting.' (F12) — a routing decision made without asking.

No traffic excuse is available for the second segment: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window (F15), and the only congestion bands on record concern PIE at band 4 (F13) and Boon Lay Way at band 5 (F14), neither of which is a band 1–2 record corroborating the substituted stretch of the optimal route at 15:16 (RD-4(a)/(b)).

Because the second segment is an unexempted off-route segment, and RydeTAXI bills by a metered distance rate so detour km enter the fare (F8: 23.80 km distance billed at $1.4101/km, i.e. $33.56), the rider is entitled to a partial refund of that segment's extra 2.63 km (F4, F5) (RD-2).

The refund amount is computable from the fare facts: 2.63 km × $1.4101/km (the trip's distance fare ÷ distance km, F5) = $3.71, refundable as refund_partial; the waiting fee of $0.11 is a meter waiting unit and is not refunded (F6).

The driver's recorded history — 1 dispute upheld in the last 90 days with 431 trips (F18) — is a profile fact offered only as the basis for an additional account-review flag if the tribunal finds the driver repeated an unexempted deviation, not as evidence that this deviation occurred (RD-6).

weaknesses: The rider's consent message (F10) is a bare 'Sure, no problem.' with no named road; the driver asked about 'Bukit Batok West Avenue 3' (F9) but no fact ties either driven segment (F3 or F4) to that road, so on the first segment the judge may find agreement scope undetermined under RD-5/G13 rather than settled, and the same looseness could be argued by the driver to stretch consent toward the second segment.

Evidence of 'jam near the start' the rider relies on is thin: the only congestion facts are PIE band 4 (F13) and Boon Lay Way band 5 (F14) plus 'no traffic incidents recorded' (F15) — band 4 is not a band 1–2 severe-congestion record, so RD-4(b) cannot alone excuse the first (or any) segment, and the driver will lean on the rider's own complaint wording ('I agreed to go round the jam at the start', F10) to claim the whole route change was sanctioned.

The driver's recorded history shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days with 0 route disputes upheld (F18), so RD-6's 'repeated route deviation' predicate is weak; the rider also has 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F17), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of contested fares.

The excess distance billed in the fare facts is 5.12 km (F5) while the two off-route segments sum to only 4.45 km (F3+F4), so part of the distance excess is unmatched corridor mileage; the driver may argue the segments are measurement artifacts rather than real detours, and F2's +11.2 min duration (partly attributable to the same congestion in F13) is not charged as detour mileage.

claims.assertion: The first off-route segment, 14:59–15:05, adding 1.82 km (F3), was expressly agreed by the rider: the driver asked at 14:56 'Jam on Pan Island Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Bukit Batok West Avenue 3?' (F9) and the rider replied at 14:56 'Sure, no problem.' (F10) — consent given before the segment start (F3), so under RD-5 this segment is exempt and no refund is due for it.

The agreement in F9/F10 is a specific named-road authorisation covering 'Bukit Batok West Avenue 3'; the material does not contain a road-name fact tying the 14:59–15:05 driven path to that road, so the reach of the consent over the first segment is at most undetermined and the case on that segment should go to a human rather than be read against the driver (G13 boundary).

A severe-congestion exception is partly evidenced for the trip window: the Pan Island Expressway was recorded at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) for 14:44–15:34 (F13) and light rain was falling (F16), which support that a reroute away from the expressway corridor was a reasonable response to traffic conditions, though F13 is a band 4 record and not band 1–2.

No traffic incident is recorded near the route during the trip window (F15), so the driver does not claim the RD-4(a) incident exemption and does not dispute that the exemption evidence for either segment is only the speed-band record.

The driver's explanation of the second deviation, that the 15:16–15:23 GPS rerouted him (F12), is a post-trip written statement only and is not rider consent; no message from the rider before 15:16 authorises that segment (F9, F10, F11 — the chat has only two messages, both at 14:56), so the second segment is not exempt under RD-5.

On the charge itself the meters are honest: excess distance billed is $7.22 for 5.12 km at $1.4101/km (F5), waiting billed is $0.11 for 0.4 min at $0.26/min (F6), and there is no surge (F7); the total $48.44 is a metered RydeTAXI fare built from base, distance, time, waiting and platform components (F8), with no unpublished add-on — so FARE-1 discloses nothing to refund beyond the metered mileage already accounted for.

If the tribunal finds the second segment unexempt, the amount computable from the fare fact is limited to that segment's extra 2.63 km (F4) × $1.4101/km (F5) = $3.71, i.e. a refund_partial of $3.71 rather than the full complaint; the first segment's 1.82 km (F3) is not on that footing because of the 14:56 agreement (F9, F10).

points.response: Conceded: we do not contest exemption of the 14:59–15:05 segment — the rider's own 14:56 message 'Sure, no problem.' (F10) precedes the segment start (F3) and is the rider's message, satisfying RD-5; our claim C2 already treated that segment as consented, and our money claim rests solely on the second segment (F4).

Even if the reach of the F9/F10 agreement over the first segment were undetermined rather than settled, that is immaterial: the rider seeks nothing for the 14:59–15:05 segment, so no segment whose result turns on that ambiguity affects the amount or any account flag, and the escalation point of G13 does not arise.

Band 4 (30–39 km/h, F13) is not a band 1–2 record and RD-4(b) bands are only corroboration, so F13 cannot by itself exempt any segment; light rain (F16) is not a named exemption in RD-4 at all, and in any event these facts say nothing about the 15:16–15:23 segment (F4).
The driver's own concession that no RD-4(a) incident exemption exists (F15) disposes of the only traffic excuse that RD-4(a) could have supplied, leaving the 15:16–15:23 segment unexempted (F4).

We agree the second segment is not exempt — the complete two-message chat record (F11, F9, F10) contains nothing before 15:16 and the driver's post-trip statement (F12) is a statement, not rider consent, exactly as RD-5 and G11 require; this concession is the basis of the refund we seek, not a reason for no_action.

FARE-1 is not the operative clause for a metered RydeTAXI detour: RD-2 expressly directs a partial refund of the unexempted segment's extra km for RydeTAXI, and the meter's honesty at $1.4101/km (F5, F8) is precisely what makes the 2.63 km of extra driving (F4) chargeable and refundable.

The respondent's own arithmetic matches ours — 2.63 km (F4) × $1.4101/km (F5) = $3.71 — so no_action is untenable while an unexempted segment (F4) exists; the only dispute left is that the driver asks for zero where the policy requires refund_partial of that computed sum (RD-2).

Our own figure stands unchanged at $3.71 for the 2.63 km second segment only (F4, F5), and we withdraw nothing from it; the first segment's 1.82 km (F3) is excluded from our claim per the conceded consent (F10).

Accepted only as a statement of the two recorded segments and their size (F3, F4); the rider's framing that both are unexempted ignores that the first is covered by the rider's own pre-segment message (F9, F10).

No dispute: I rely on the same facts — the driver's 14:56 question naming Bukit Batok West Avenue 3 (F9) and the rider's 14:56 'Sure, no problem.' (F10, F11) sent before the 14:59 segment start (F3) — and this reinforces D1 that the first segment is exempt under RD-5.

I do not need the traffic limb for the first segment, and I concede F13 is only band 4, which RD-4(b) treats as corroboration and not a standalone exemption; the first segment stands on the rider's own consent under RD-5, not on RD-4.

This is already my own position (D5): the complete two-message chat, both at 14:56 (F11, F9, F10), contains nothing before the 15:16 start of F4, and the driver's post-trip statement that his GPS rerouted him (F12) is not rider consent under RD-5 and loses to the GPS record.

Conceded on the second segment: no incident is recorded near the route (F15), and the only bands are PIE band 4 and Boon Lay Way band 5 (F13, F14), neither of which is a band 1–2 record tied to the substituted stretch at 15:16, so RD-4 does not exempt F4.

Conceded as to segment two only: F4 adds 2.63 km on a metered RydeTAXI fare (F8 bills 23.80 km at $1.4101/km), so that segment is refundable under RD-2, but the rider's claim that both segments are unexempted fails because F3 is covered by F9/F10 under RD-5.

The arithmetic is agreed as far as segment two goes — 2.63 km × $1.4101/km = $3.71 (F4, F5) — and I adopt that figure as the ceiling of my client's exposure; what I do not accept is the rider's implication that the first segment's 1.82 km (F3) is refundable at all, and the waiting unit of $0.11 (F6) is correctly not claimed back.
Accepted that F18 can only support an additional action and not the finding, and I note the route sub-count in F18 is zero (0 route disputes upheld) so the RD-6 predicate is not met here.
